abstract.text: Carry your own data on entities and in globals, alongside the engine’s closed core.

inlineContent.text: The engine only ever branches on a closed set of traits and scalar globals, and that is what keeps its behavior auditable: every decision it can make is visible in a handful of small enums. Your game’s own data does not have to live in that set. A wallet, a set of combat stats, an item’s price — custom state and custom traits ride along type-erased through the same storage the engine already saves and restores, read by your rules and by nothing else.

try reply("Sold. You have \(purse.coins) coins left.")

Those bytes are the reason to touch a struct global once per rule body rather than field by field. Reading one decodes and writing one encodes, so
